newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rice steady this week, uptrend likely - trade.
newsitem.headline: Thai rice steady this week, uptrend likely - trade.

text.p: Thai rice prices were mostly steady this week with a bias towards an uptrend as deliveries to customers picked up, trade sources said on Friday.

Vessels were loading about 80,000 tonnes of rice for deliveries to destinations in Asia and Africa, mostly to China. Fresh supplies which entered the market were offset by demand to cover obligations, they tol Reuters.
An additional 200,000 tonnes were expected to be shipped from now until the end of this year. The government expects 1996 rice exports to reach 5.2 million tonnes.
"The demand supported the prices which I think could move a bit higher next week," one trader said.
The Thai benchmark 100 percent B grade was quoted around US$305-350 per tonne FOB Bangkok and 100 percent fragrant rice was quoted at $615 per tonne on the same basis, barely changed from last week.
Some traders raised questions about the Commerce Ministry's daily rice loading report which indicated some amountd of rice were being shipped to Vietnam and Burma.
"It is very unlikely. First of all, I don't think these countries allow rice imports. Besides, their crops this year are quite okay," said one trader.
Other industry sources said the vessels the ministry had said were destined for the two countries would actually go to China and Indonesia.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) forecast that Burma would produce 18 million tonnes of rice for 1996/97 season (Apr-Mar) and export about 300,000 tonnes.
On the govenment side, talks to secure rice deals for 1997 with potential clients continued with the head of Commerce Ministry's foreign trade department scheduled to leave for Manila on Monday.
"So far it looks good but further negotiation is needed. I can't tell you much at this point as it could affect prices and subsequently derail the talks," a ministry source said.

Among the countries to which the commerce ministry plans to send sales teams between now and February are Japan, the Philippines, China, Indonesia, Malaysia and some African and Middle Eastern countries.
